card.name: Intolerant/intolerable in dosing text
card.fires_on: The middle of the word intolerant, intolerable or intolerance (the pieces 'intoler' and 'oler'), mostly in dose-adjustment text. Weaker on 'outweigh' and 'benefit' in dosing sentences.

modes.label: Intolerable reactions
modes.description: Partway through 'intolerable' in dose-modification tables for adverse reactions.
modes.example: Withhold OMCAZIO for: Int<<oler>>able Grade 2 adverse reactions Grade

modes.label: Intolerant patients
modes.description: The 'intoler' piece of 'intolerant' or 'intolerance' describing patients who cannot take a drug.

modes.label: Other dosing words
modes.description: Occasional words like 'outweigh' or 'benefit' in dosing or risk statements.
modes.example: Some patients may<< benefit>> from a dosage of 300

card.writes: It seems to push toward rare word completions, but the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It lights up on the word 'intolerable' or 'intolerant' when labels discuss patients who cannot tolerate a drug or its side effects.
